questions.Question (ask verbatim): Our pigment supplier sells us a 'D&C Red lake blend' in a castor-oil carrier. How do FDA's definitions classify the lake, the blend and the oil?
questions.Key Answer Elements: 70.3(l): a lake is a straight color extended on a substratum by adsorption, coprecipitation or chemical combination, not simple mixing. (j): straight colors (listed in parts 73, 74 and 81) include lakes. (k): a mixture is two or more straight colors, or straight colors plus diluents. (m): the castor oil, if not itself a color additive and intentionally mixed to facilitate use, is a diluent.

questions.Section Heading: Color additives in standardized foods and new drugs.
questions.Focus: Color additive proposals in new drug applications and food standards
questions.Question (ask verbatim): Our cosmetics company is filing a new drug application for a tinted acne gel that uses an unlisted colorant purely for color. Does Part 70 say anything about that?
questions.Key Answer Elements: Yes. 70.10(b)(1): if a new drug application proposes a color additive for coloring purposes only, part 71 safety-information requirements apply unless previously submitted or safety for that use is established. (b)(2): if the application inferentially proposes a color additive without designating it, the Commissioner notifies the applicant and proceeds under part 71. (b)(3): the color additive petition's filing date is the new drug application's filing date.

questions.Question (ask verbatim): We're petitioning to list a new pigment for cosmetics. It shares a component with an already-listed colorant. Will FDA consider that overlap in setting a tolerance?
questions.Key Answer Elements: Yes. 70.11(a)-(c): different color additives, and food additives and pesticide chemicals, may cause similar or related pharmacological or biological effects and, absent evidence to the contrary, are presumed to have additive toxic effects. (d): in setting tolerances the Commissioner considers, among other things, the amount of any common component permitted in other color additives, in food additives and pesticide chemical residues, and similar biological activity (e.g., cholinesterase inhibition).

questions.Question (ask verbatim): We're petitioning to list a new colorant for cosmetics only. What deposit is due, and what if we withdraw?
questions.Key Answer Elements: 70.19(c): $2,600.00 for drugs and/or cosmetics only (vs. $3,000.00 general or foods only under (a)-(b)), regardless of tolerances or restrictions (d). Withdrawal before acceptance: refund less $600.00 clerical fee (e). Withdrawal within 30 days after filing: refund reduced by $1,600.00 for (c) petitions (f). Resubmission within 6 months of a post-filing withdrawal: $1,600.00 for (c); later, full deposit (g). Resubmission after pre-acceptance withdrawal: full new deposit (h).

questions.Section Heading: Packaging requirements for straight colors (other than hair dyes).
questions.Question (ask verbatim): We repack certified straight colors into smaller pails for cosmetic customers. What packaging rules apply?
questions.Key Answer Elements: 70.20: straight colors (other than hair dyes) must be packaged in containers that prevent changes in composition, sealed so they cannot be opened without breaking the seal. An unavoidable moisture-content change from ordinary, customary exposure under good storage, packing and distribution is not a change in composition. Packaging material that is a food additive must be authorized by an appropriate regulation in parts 170 through 189.

questions.Question (ask verbatim): Our cosmetic use is in a petition alongside food uses, but the data don't show all uses would be safe at the levels proposed. What happens?
questions.Key Answer Elements: 70.45: if the data fail to show safety for all proposed uses or levels, the Commissioner publishes a Federal Register notice that the safe tolerance must be allocated among competing needs, calling for data from all interested persons under section 721(b)(8). Time for acting is stayed until the data are presented, then runs anew. As promptly as possible, the Commissioner announces the allocation and tolerance limitations by order.

questions.Focus: FDA requests for samples/information and effect on time limits
questions.Question (ask verbatim): While reviewing our color additive petition, FDA asked for samples of our pigment and the finished eyeshadow. Must we provide them, and does this affect the review timeline?
questions.Key Answer Elements: Under 71.4 FDA may, at any time during review, request samples of the additive, its components, or the cosmetic containing it, and clarifying information, stating the quantity needed. The 90-day limit under section 721(d)(1) is extended one day per day from the request's mailing date until response. If not submitted within 180 days after filing, when requested reasonably in advance, the petition is considered withdrawn without prejudice.

questions.Section Heading: Extension of time for studying petitions; substantive amendments; withdrawal of petitions without prejudice.
questions.Question (ask verbatim): FDA told us our technically complete petition is inadequate because some data are unclear. Can we pull it without hurting a future filing?
questions.Key Answer Elements: Yes. Under 71.6(c)(1), when FDA notifies the petitioner that a technically complete petition is inadequate (e.g., data unclear or incomplete), the petitioner may withdraw it pending clarification or additional data, without prejudice to a future filing; on refiling, the time limitation begins anew. Under (c)(2) a petitioner may also withdraw without prejudice any time before the 71.20 order is forwarded to the Federal Register.

questions.Focus: Content and timing of listing regulation; exemption by order
questions.Question (ask verbatim): If FDA grants our petition for a new cosmetic color, what will the listing regulation look like and when will it publish?
questions.Key Answer Elements: Within 90 days after filing (180 if extended under section 721(d)(1)), FDA forwards a regulation listing the additive in part 73 or 74 to the Federal Register. Under (a)(1) it may list for general use or prescribe conditions: specific products or classes, maximum straight color or diluent, manner of use, and directions, labeling or packing requirements. (a)(2) lists only uses found suitable and safe; otherwise an order denying with reasons.

questions.Section Heading: Deception as a basis for refusing to issue regulations; deceptive use of a color additive for which a regulation has issued.
questions.Focus: Deceptive use of a listed color
questions.Question (ask verbatim): Our foundation uses a listed color additive at a higher level to hide discoloration that develops as the product degrades. The color is listed for cosmetics. Is that covered by the listing?
questions.Key Answer Elements: No. Under 71.22 a regulation authorizing a color additive generally in or on a cosmetic does not authorize its use in a manner that may promote deception or conceal damage or inferiority. Such use is considered a use for which no regulation has issued under section 721(b), even if a regulation covers other uses. 71.22 gives no compliance determination for a specific product.

questions.Section Heading: Procedure for filing objections to regulations.
questions.Focus: Objections and hearings on color regulations
questions.Question (ask verbatim): FDA just issued a color additive regulation that bars eye-area use of a pigment we rely on. How do we object or seek a hearing?
questions.Key Answer Elements: Under 71.30(a), objections and hearings relating to color additive regulations under section 721(b) and (c) of the Act are governed by parts 10, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 19 of chapter I. Under 71.30(b), the fees specified in § 70.19 apply. 71.30 itself sets no deadline or content; those come from the listed parts.

questions.Section Heading: Exemption of color additives for investigational use.
questions.Question (ask verbatim): We want to ship test mascaras containing an unlisted color additive to an outside safety lab. Is there an exemption, and what labeling and records are required?
questions.Key Answer Elements: Under 71.37(a), shipments of a color additive, or a cosmetic containing it, for investigational use by experts qualified to investigate safety are exempt from sections 402(c), 501(a) and 601(e) if prominently labeled: "Caution—Contains new color additive—For investigational use only." Under (b), the shipper keeps records of the expert's name and post-office address, date, quantity, and batch or code mark for 2 years, available for inspection and copying on request.
